steps.name: Sample structure QC
caveats: Fractional values in this 'counts' table mean the delivered values are not raw counts (e.g. Salmon TPM/scaledTPM). No average transcript length table and no per-sample quantification files exist, so downstream steps must fit the count model on the values as delivered with no length offset, and the report must state that the length offset is lost and that a change in isoform use can show as differential expression.
Do not run tximport on a gene-level table — tximport imports transcript estimates — and do not invent a length input.
steps.context: Inputs: /eval-four-models-v2-with-paired-3groups-n4-s1-1/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv (12,000 genes x 12 samples, 13 columns including the gene-name column) and /eval-four-models-v2-with-paired-3groups-n4-s1-1/data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv (12 rows: subject, condition; each of 4 subjects contributes exactly one control, one treated_a, one treated_b). Counts are gene-level from Salmon with the length-correction state undocumented. Before QC: (1) verify the 12 sample columns match the 12 metadata rows one-to-one; (2) verify rows are genes, not transcripts — if row names look transcript-level, stop and report rather than aggregating silently; (3) check whether values are integers or fractional to document the import state; (4) report library size per sample. QC itself: variance-stabilizing transformation blind to the design, PCA on the 500 most variable genes, Euclidean distance heatmap, all colored by subject and by condition.
steps.question: Do the 12 samples (4 subjects x 3 conditions: control, treated_a, treated_b) import cleanly from counts.csv and metadata.csv, and do they cluster by subject and condition before any test runs?

grounding.reason: Sample structure QC: vst(blind), PCA, sample distances, library sizes per R-0033@40bf

steps.description: Verifies the Salmon-derived 12,000 x 12 gene count table against the 12-row sample metadata, documents the import state, and produces blind-vst PCA plus a distance heatmap colored by subject and condition.
acceptance_criteria: PCA and sample distance heatmap produced and saved, colored by subject and condition
Every sample assigned to exactly one subject x condition cell consistent with metadata.csv, or any departure (mismatched sample, outlier sample) explicitly flagged
Library size per sample reported; import state (integer counts vs fractional values) documented in the step output
Rows confirmed to be genes (or a transcript-level row problem reported, which halts the plan)

steps.name: DESeq2 LRT + pairwise Wald contrasts
caveats: Import state is not established: the quantifier name Salmon alone does not prove a length correction occurred, and no per-sample quantification files (quant.sf, abundance.h5, genes.results) or average transcript length table per gene and sample are present. Fit the count model on the counts as delivered, with no length offset, and carry the statement that the length offset is lost and a change in isoform use can show as differential expression into the report.
The treated_a vs treated_b contrast is a contrast of two coefficients: shrink it with ashr, not apeglm (apeglm accepts a single coefficient only).
Do not filter results by unadjusted p-value or by a post-hoc fold-change cutoff; the question is any response, so test against the zero null with no lfcThreshold.
With only 4 replicates per condition cell, expect some genes flagged as count outliers with NA p-values; report their count and inspect any flagged gene that matters to the question.
steps.context: Counts as validated in T1S1 (12,000 genes x 12 samples; pre-filter keeps a gene with at least 10 counts in at least 4 samples, the smallest group size; no stricter pre-filter). Design formula ~ subject + condition with subject (4 levels) first as the blocking term, condition with explicit reference level control set by relevel before model fitting. No pre-normalization: DESeq2 median-of-ratios size factors are applied inside the negative binomial model. (1) Omnibus 'responds to either treatment' test: likelihood ratio test, full ~ subject + condition vs reduced ~ subject, p-values BH-adjusted within that test. (2) Named pairwise Wald contrasts as (factor, numerator, denominator) triples: (condition, treated_a, control), (condition, treated_b, control), (condition, treated_a, treated_b); the A vs B contrast is a two-coefficient contrast, not one coefficient of the model. (3) lfcShrink with ashr for each contrast — ashr accepts the two-coefficient contrast; apeglm accepts a single coefficient only. (4) results() with alpha = 0.05 and DESeq2 independent filtering on; the LRT also adjusted at this alpha. (5) Histogram of unadjusted p-values per test, inspected before trusting the adjusted values. (6) With 4 replicates per condition cell, DESeq2 flags count outliers via Cook's distance and sets those genes' p-values to NA (replace behavior only applies at 7+ replicates per cell) — count and report them separately from independent-filtering NAs.
steps.question: Which genes respond to either treatment within subject (treated_a or treated_b vs control), and does treatment A differ from treatment B?

grounding.reason: DESeq2 likelihood ratio test per R-0029@22ca

steps.description: DESeq2 two-factor model (~ subject + condition, reference level control) with an LRT omnibus test for 'responds to either treatment' within subject and three named pairwise Wald contrasts including treated_a vs treated_b; ashr-shrunk log fold changes; BH FDR within each contrast at alpha 0.05.
acceptance_criteria: One LRT result table (genes responding to either treatment) and three pairwise Wald result tables (treated_a vs control, treated_b vs control, treated_a vs treated_b), each carrying log2FoldChange, shrunken_log2FoldChange (ashr), lfcSE, stat, pvalue, padj, with the contrast name on every row
Number of genes tested after pre-filtering and number of DE genes per test at padj < 0.05 reported
P-value histogram per test saved and its shape assessed before the adjusted p-values are trusted
Number of genes with NA p-value from count-outlier flagging reported separately from independent-filtering NAs
'Responds to either treatment' gene list defined as LRT padj < 0.05 and labeled as such

steps.name: Report with edgeR robustness
caveats: FDR control holds per contrast, not across the set of contrasts — state this, and pair every adjusted p-value and gene list with its contrast name.
The gene table and plots rank on the shrunken log fold change only; the ranked list for any future enrichment would use the test statistic, not a fold change.
Do not present the union of the DESeq2 and edgeR significant sets as the result.
steps.context: Assemble the final report from T1S1/T1S2 outputs: (1) Methods header — DESeq2 1.52.0, design ~ subject + condition, explicit reference level control, the three named contrasts plus the LRT, alpha 0.05, BH adjustment scope (within contrast), number of genes tested after filtering, number of DE genes per test, and the caveat that the Salmon length offset is lost because the import state was not established. (2) Fit diagnostics before the gene tables: MA plot and dispersion plot for the LRT and each contrast. (3) Gene tables with unshranked log2FoldChange, ashr-shrunken log2FoldChange (estimator named in the header), and lfcSE; genes ranked and plotted on the shrunken value; p-values kept from the unshrunken fit; every gene list paired with its contrast name. (4) Robustness: run edgeR (glmQLFit/glmQLFTest, design ~ subject + condition, reference level control, same pre-filter) on the same counts; report the number of significant genes per method per contrast and the size of the intersection; treat the intersection as the high-confidence set and list genes called by only one method as a secondary set labeled with that method; never present the union as the result. (5) Reproducibility record: sessionInfo, package versions, random seed, design, thresholds, and a statement of the data's annotation/identifier state (gene symbols as delivered, no annotation release pinned).
steps.question: What must the final report contain so a reader can reproduce the within-subject treatment effects and judge their robustness?
constraints: report: report_fields = method, versions, design, thresholds, n_tested, n_de, session_info (doi:10.1093/bib/bbz124)
report: reproducibility_record = session_info, seed, package_versions, collection_version, annotation_release (doi:10.1371/journal.pcbi.1003285)
steps.description: Final report: methods, fit diagnostics, gene tables with shrunken and unshranked log fold changes, DESeq2 vs edgeR quasi-likelihood robustness overlap, and the reproducibility record.
acceptance_criteria: Report states method, package versions, design formula, reference level, each contrast, alpha, n genes tested, and n DE genes per test
MA plot and dispersion plot appear before the gene tables, with a one-line statement of what each shows
Gene tables carry unshranked log2FoldChange, ashr-shrunken log2FoldChange, and lfcSE, ranked by the shrunken value
DESeq2 vs edgeR quasi-likelihood overlap reported per contrast, with the intersection labeled as the high-confidence set and single-method genes labeled by method
sessionInfo, seed, and package versions stored with the results

plan.title: Paired 3-arm DE: treatments vs control and A vs B
plan.analytical_narrative: The design is paired within subject: 4 subjects, each with one sample each under control, treated_a, and treated_b (12 samples total, single batch), from a 12,000-gene Salmon-derived count table of human blood. The research question has two parts: (1) which genes respond to either treatment within subject — answered by a DESeq2 likelihood ratio test with the subject as a blocking term (full design ~ subject + condition vs reduced ~ subject), which finds genes differing between any of the three conditions within subjects; and (2) whether the two treatments differ from each other — answered by named pairwise Wald contrasts (treated_a vs control, treated_b vs control, and the two-coefficient contrast treated_a vs treated_b) from the same model. Because the quantifier is Salmon but the import state is undocumented (no per-sample quantification files, no average transcript length table), the model is fit on the counts as delivered with no length offset, and the report must state that the length offset is lost and that isoform-use changes can masquerade as differential expression. Log fold changes are shrunken with ashr (required for the two-coefficient A vs B contrast, which apeglm cannot take), p-values are BH-adjusted within each contrast at alpha 0.05 with DESeq2 independent filtering on, and the report carries a robustness check against edgeR quasi-likelihood on the same counts and design. The dataset is tiny (12,000 x 12), so all steps run on minimal resources.

flags.message: A quantifier name alone does not establish that the length correction occurred. If the counts come from Salmon, kallisto, or RSEM as a gene-level table, with no per-sample quantification files and no average transcript length table, the import state is not established. Ask for the per-sample quantification files, quant.sf, abundance.h5, or genes.results, or for the average transcript length table per gene and sample. If neither arrives, fit the count model on the counts as delivered, with no length offset, and state in the plan and in the report that the length offset is lost and that a change in isoform use can show as differential expression. Do not run tximport on a gene table, because tximport imports transcript estimates, and do not invent a length input.
